items.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996
items.q: And there was an old man from Pittsburgh, no from Pennsylvania called Weinberg, and you’d do the Weinberg tour. He was the agent.

ctx.x: It was standard, but I had not been exposed to that. I used to go down and sometimes spend a summer I guess I did it about five times with my great grandmother, who was in Wilmington, North Carolina, but I was too young to understand that because you know we never really had to go out from a certain area. And going down by train there was a Traveler’s Aid, I think you wore a little button or something like that and you’d stop in Philadelphia and someone would come on and make sure you got some milk and cookies ©…

or something, and get to wash. They’d take care of you, you know. So when I went with Bostic, we would go out sometimes like three months, we’d do it sometimes twice a year — three month tour. And one-nighters. And there was an old man from Pittsburgh, no from Pennsylvania called Weinberg, and you’d do the Weinberg tour.
